what: SURF-v2's frozen analysis configuration (surf_v2/REGISTRATION.md; the research plan revision/SURF_V2_PLAN.md sections 4.3-4.7 and its addendum revision/SURF_V2_EVAL.md). surf_v2/analysis.py and surf_v2/qrule.py read nothing else that decides a result.
deployed_tau_note: the deployed networks at their published tau: the studies' at d = 7-15 (weights/configs.json), R17's 4.539173126220703 (q = 8 %) at d = 17 (weights/configs_sv2.json d17_b5_r787_q08)

qrule.source: ising-arch:ising_compare/arch/policy.py fit (lines 117-165), executed as written: tau_q = float(np.quantile(|c|, q)) for q > 0 (numpy's default interpolation on the float32 |c|), tau_0 = 0; a shot is routed when |c| < tau_q (float32 |c| against tau_q); r_q = routed / N; F_cal(q) = failures with the routed shots taking correlated PM's calibration answer; admissible when projected(q) <= bar; limit L = M - 2 sqrt(2 M); the smallest admissible q with F_cal(q) <= L, else the fallback of the distance's registered policy (fallback): the largest admissible q at d = 7, the admissible q with the fewest calibration failures (ties: the smaller q) at d = 9-17; no admissible q: no policy (the network alone, labelled)

7.source: ising-arch:ising_compare/data/arch/g6_path_d7_r740.json (sha256 db334a71ae833ef227d89bbfbc5ab67981f01dae18a1310710e08ebce10bd5dd): measured complete paths, router included, locked before the d = 7 fit (arch/README.md 15.7)

qrule.cost: frontier projection: projected(0) = net_us; projected(q) = net_us + router_us + r_q x cost(q), cost(q) = the mean over the shots routed at q of correlated PM's time per shot on the calibration set (one pinned core of an EPYC 7713 node, surf_v2/calcost.py), converted to the Grace basis by the CPU term's ratio G(d) / (the same node's correlated PM per block on validation chunk 0, median of three; timing/cpu_term.py ref)
qrule.fallback_source: each distance's registered policy (registered_choices policy_file, checked by sha256 in qrule reproduce): at d = 7 policy_d7s9_r740.json, fitted on 2 October 18:06 PDT before G7 (ising-arch README 16.1, registered 19:12) with the rule 'else the largest admissible q' (policy.py fit --fallback largest), which G7 left as it was because the policy met the limit; at d = 9-17 the policies' fallback 'argmin' (README 16.1). The research plan's 4.3 wrote argmin at every d; at d = 7 this is the registered policy's rule instead (SURF_V2_EVAL.md section 9)

registered_choices.what: the studies' registered choices that surf_v2/qrule.py reproduce must give from their calibration records (Alpine /scratch/alpine/$USER/ising_arch/out/policy); q, tau, routed shots, calibration failures, projected time and whether the choice met the limit, as the policies recorded them

ising_label: Ising accuracy read with NVIDIA's official PyTorch numerics only (no TensorRT plan); Ising's speed is the studies' historical TensorRT composite

A.what: the new pair against each baseline, accuracy
A.test: exact two-sided McNemar test on the discordant shots and Newcombe's method-8 interval of LER(pair) - LER(baseline) at 1 - alpha (convlines.stats.paired)
A.verdict: better when p < alpha and the whole interval lies below 0; else not shown

B.what: the new pair against each baseline, speed
B.test: the pair's composite time strictly below the baseline's registered time on the Grace basis; no statistical test
B.verdict: holds or not; 'not established (timing session not qualified)' when no session qualified

C.what: new against deployed, per d: each network alone (q = 0), and each pair at its own q (the deployed at its published tau)
C.test: exact two-sided McNemar test, Holm over the tests of the six distances (12, fewer under a training-failure exception); Newcombe 95 % interval reported beside it (pointwise, not simultaneous)
C.verdict: better (worse) when Holm rejects and the new network fails on fewer (more) shots; else inconclusive, reported as inconclusive and never as 'no difference'

families.claim: a distance's claim against the baselines holds when all 16 of its comparisons in A and B hold (intersection-union, no further correction); C reports both directions

registered_times_us.what: each baseline's registered time per shot on the Grace basis (release main: timing.composite rows from results/, and results/controls_speed.json grace_us at d = 7-15 for Ising + correlated PM, the post hoc controls; study 4's registered opponents at d = 17); surf_v2/tests check them against those files

nvidia_basis_d17.what: described only: d = 17 on the NVIDIA-distance basis (timing/R17_GRACE_NOTE.md, the table of R17's cells): every CPU time converted at d = 17 by NVIDIA's distance-specific values; ours' CPU term by G'(17) = 860.71 us over the node's correlated PM per block

registered_composites_us.what: the deployed networks' registered composites at their published tau (README section 4; d = 17: R17's), shown beside the same networks timed again in this session

timing.gpu_check: surf_v2/gpucheck.py at the session's start and end: 1 GiB held, 3 s of fp16 matrix products, nvidia-smi every 100 ms: median SM clock >= 97 % of the maximum, throttle reasons none or idle, no other process on the GPU before, during or after, under 64 MiB in use before
timing.qualification: a session qualifies when its GPU check passes at the start and at the end and every network, new and deployed, has five accepted GPU-term processes and its accepted handoff process(es) within two replacements; a third rejected process of any network, a failed GPU check or a lost pod disqualifies it; at most two sessions, the second only after a technical failure, on a new secure host, timing every network again; the first qualifying session counts; if neither qualifies, the second's accepted processes are reported as unqualified and family B as 'not established (timing session not qualified)'

pair_curves.what: described: each network's pair failures on the test set at every q of its distance's grid, tau_q fitted on the new calibration set (the rule's tau_q), new and deployed side by side; and the calibration frontiers (F_cal(q) against the projected time) of the new networks

paper_rows.rule: the paper's surface rows are the new networks' pairs at every distance, whatever their results (D4); the one exception is a distance under the training-failure exception of the freeze (freeze.json exceptions), whose row is the deployed network's pair read on the fresh test set, labelled as the exception; the deployed networks' registered results stay in the provenance table as the earlier tests

dry.what: dry runs only (never a result): the sv2dry set stands in for both the calibration and the test set
